agentCan: Build the authorize URL (always including the offline scope), code exchange, and rotating refresh storage

approval.cost: No fee for registering an app or using OAuth is stated in the docs read
approval.trigger: No app review, approval, verification, or marketplace/listing process is described in the official Typeform developer documentation read. Apps are registered self-service inside your own Typeform account (under your organization's Developer Apps), and once registered, any Typeform user can be sent through the authorize URL and grant access on the consent screen. The docs state no pre-approval user/install cap, no listing process, and no fee for registering an app or using OAuth.

blockers.detail: 'To receive a refresh token in the first place, your application must pass an extra offline scope during the authorization code request', and the scopes page repeats: 'Always add the offline scope to receive a refresh token.' Miss it and every user must re-run the full OAuth flow when their access token expires (default 1 week). This is the single most important setup decision, and it happens at first authorization.
blockers.howToClear: Include offline in every authorize request from day one.
blockers.title: No offline scope = no refresh token, ever

blockers.detail: 'For security purposes, the refresh procedure will invalidate the old refresh token.' Each refresh returns a new refresh token, so you must persist the newest value after every refresh; replaying a stale refresh token will fail. Refresh can only narrow scope: scope is a 'Space-delimited list that narrows the extent of access that your newly obtained token requires. You cannot ask for a wider scope than your initial authorization request scope.'
blockers.howToClear: Persist the newest refresh token atomically on every refresh.
blockers.title: Refresh tokens rotate; refresh can only narrow

blockers.detail: 'After you save your app, the app's client_secret will be shown only once.' Unlike a hard one-way door, Typeform documents a recovery path: regenerate it from the Edit app panel (Edit app > Regenerate client secret). The docs don't state whether regeneration instantly kills existing tokens; don't assume.
blockers.howToClear: Store the secret at registration; regenerate via Edit app if it is lost or compromised.
blockers.title: client_secret is shown once (but regenerable)

sources.label: Create applications that integrate with Typeform's APIs (registration, authorize/token endpoints, 1-week default tokens, rotation, offline scope)
OAuth 2.0 scopes for your applications (resource:action scopes; 'Always add the offline scope')
Personal access token (tfp_ tokens; GitHub secret scanning auto-disable)

tested: Read-only verification: the application model, endpoints, token behavior, and the absence of any review process were checked against developer.typeform.com (typeform.com/developers) (no app registered, nothing submitted)
unverified: Refresh token expiry/lifetime (rotation and invalidation are documented; no maximum lifetime is given).
Whether the access-token lifetime can be configured away from the stated 1-week default (the docs call 1 week the 'default' but describe no setting to change it).
Any cap on the number of apps per account/organization or users per app, and any fees (none stated).
Any app review or listing program (none described in the developer documentation; if Typeform runs a partner/listing process, it is not documented on the pages read).

alternatives: Personal Access Token (PAT): a per-user token (values prefixed tfp_) generated in the user's account under Account > Personal tokens, with scopes chosen at generation time. Typeform positions it for direct access ('for example, with cURL or Postman'); it acts only as the user who generated it, so a multi-user SaaS would have to ask every user to generate and paste a PAT, a manual onboarding model, not a connect flow. Security note: Typeform 'is a Github secret scanning partner... any Typeform personal access token added to a repository will be detected by Github. Once detected, it will automatically be disabled'
flavor.recommended: A standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code app, always including the offline scope so you receive a refresh token
flavor.why: The object is an application registered inside a Typeform account, in the admin panel under Organization > Developer Apps ('Register a new app'), yielding a client_id and client_secret. Typeform 'uses OAuth 2.0 to secure the endpoints for the Create, Responses, and Webhooks APIs'; every API request passes the access token in the Authorization header (the Embed SDK is the exception; it needs no token). Authorize URL: api.typeform.com/oauth/authorize; token URL: api.typeform.com/oauth/token. Scopes are resource:action pairs (accounts:read, forms:read/forms:write, responses:read/responses:write, webhooks:read/webhooks:write, workspaces:read/workspaces:write, images:read/images:write, themes:read/themes:write) and are listed on the consent screen the user sees.

humanMust: Log in to your Typeform account and register the app (Organization > Developer Apps: App Name, App website, Redirect URI(s))
Copy the client_secret immediately (shown only once; the client_id remains visible)
name: Typeform
nuances: Tokens are full-trust bearers within their scopes: 'Anyone with the access token can read, update, and delete your app users' typeforms and data, so keep access and refresh tokens and client_id and client_secret codes safe!', and never commit them to source control.

Consent is per-user and scope-explicit: the scopes you request are enumerated on the consent screen, and access applies to the authorizing user's account (forms, responses, workspaces they can access). 'The default expiration period for the access tokens is 1 week' (the token response also carries an expires_in value in seconds).

Redirect URI hygiene: HTTPS is recommended; if used, 'your SSL/TLS certificate must be validated; self-signed certificates will not work', and the redirect_uri sent to the token endpoint must match the one used at authorization (it is 'Used only for verification'). The optional state parameter provides XSRF protection and is echoed back with the code.

PAT contrast: personal access tokens are scoped at generation, can be regenerated or deleted by the user at any time from their account settings, and are auto-disabled if leaked into a GitHub repository via secret scanning.
prerequisites: A Typeform account (organization) for Developer Apps
An HTTPS redirect URI with a publicly valid certificate
The offline scope included in the first authorization request

steps.detail: Log in to your Typeform account, open the organization drop-down > Developer Apps, and 'Register a new app': App Name, App website, and Redirect URI(s); click Register app. Copy the client_secret immediately ('After you save your app, the app's client_secret will be shown only once'); the client_id remains visible in the Developer Apps panel.
steps.title: Register the app

steps.detail: GET api.typeform.com/oauth/authorize with client_id, redirect_uri, scope (space-delimited, required, and always including offline), and optional state for XSRF protection. The user logs in and grants or denies on the consent screen (scopes are enumerated there). You receive the temporary authorization code on your redirect URI with state echoed back.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize (include offline)

steps.detail: POST api.typeform.com/oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, and the same redirect_uri. The JSON response (per RFC 6749) contains token_type (always Bearer), access_token, expires_in, and a refresh_token ONLY if you specified the offline scope.
steps.title: Exchange the code

steps.detail: Call the Create/Responses/Webhooks APIs with Authorization: Bearer on every request. Access tokens expire after 1 week by default.
steps.title: Call the APIs

steps.detail: POST to the token URL with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret, and an optional scope that may only narrow the original grant. 'The response... will always include the refresh_token parameter, which will contain the newly generated refresh token', and 'the refresh procedure will invalidate the old refresh token', so persist the new one.
steps.title: Refresh (rotating)

tagline: Self-service OAuth with no review and long-lived tokens (1-week access tokens by default), where the entire integration hinges on one checkbox-equivalent: request the offline scope or you will never receive a refresh token.

time.active: ~5 min of registration + ~1 hr of flow code
